generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at max(compact)+1; unique per table; never NULL; for composite PKs generate tuples that do not collide with pre-existing compact tuples; never apply aggregate/group/dup transforms to PK columns.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Draw from the parent table's FINAL key pool (compact + generated, after all parent-side dedup/PK assignment); never NULL for NOT NULL FK columns; for nullable FK columns ~10% NULL (>=1 row per instance). At least one parent PK value is excluded from the draw pool per (parent, child-FK) pair so it stays childless in that child table. FK values are filled AFTER parent keys are final and are never overwritten by later re-planting; if a later step must change an FK column, re-fill from the final parent pool. FK columns are populated in a dedicated fill phase that runs after all non-FK columns exist; the row count for a table whose columns are all FKs (e.g. follows) is taken from table_sizes_per_instance, not from any column array.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric: Uniform integer in [min,max] from statistics; plant each listed boundary literal and one step on each side; boundary literals are guaranteed to appear (not probabilistic).
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_text: Short strings; for LIKE columns plant the exact literal, a prefix variant, a case variant, and one near variant (~30% of fresh rows carry a planted match); literals are per-column (see per_column_exceptions), never a global default.
generic_sampling_rules.char_text: Padded to declared length; plant exact and near-variant matches for LIKE literals; length <= declared length.
generic_sampling_rules.datetime: Random timestamps within the column's declared range (see semantic rules); force at least two rows to share one timestamp (tie) for ORDER columns; NULL ~10% for nullable date columns.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For nullable columns ~10% NULL (>=1 row per column per instance); plant NULLs after all dedup/filter steps; never NULL primary keys or NOT NULL columns; a planted NULL is never replaced to satisfy a rule.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicates: For distinct-share columns target 20-50% duplicate share among non-null rows; verify post-write and adjust by adding/removing duplicates; never apply to primary-key columns.

uncertainty: No calculated columns and no date pairs exist; createdate range rule is inferred from two compact values (2018) and is marked uncertain (not a hard constraint). NULL shares estimated at ~10% for nullable columns; compact rows kept and never deleted or modified. table_sizes_per_instance is a fixed per-instance size (8/9/10); the program must generate exactly these counts and ensure per-column targets remain achievable at that size. Sampling must plant NULLs, ties, duplicates, group-size histograms, boundary literals and childless parents on the FINAL arrays after dedup and FK fill; FK columns are filled from the final parent key pool and never overwritten by later re-planting; follows composite PK collisions must be avoided against compact tuples in the plan before insert. The follows table has only FK columns; its row count must come from table_sizes_per_instance and its column dict must be initialized empty before FK fill. Aggregate/group/dup transforms must never be applied to primary-key columns (tweets.id, user_profiles.uid). The f2 domain {-1,1} conflicts with the FK reference to user_profiles.uid; resolution: ensure user_profiles.uid includes -1 and 1 so the f2 pool restricted to {-1,1} is nonempty and both values appear. Post-write verification must confirm: every non-NULL FK value exists in the parent table; at least one parent has zero children in tweets.uid and at least one has zero children in follows.f1 (independently); child-count histogram contains 1, 2 and >=3; f2 subset of {-1,1} with both present; followers contains 999/1000/1001; createdate ties within 2018; duplicate shares 20-50% on email and tweets.uid; followers-per-partition distinct values. Fail the unit or replant on non-FK columns only when a target is unmet.
